- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 2–5% to forecast if recent 5-day avg > 70.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates mean reversion; if 10-day avg is > 70, forecast should be capped at 72–74.
- If model forecast is > 75 and sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; if 3-day avg is falling, forecast should be adjusted downward by 2–4%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate volatility in early days; smooth first 5–7 days by averaging with prior 5-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive and price is near 70, model often underestimates upward bias; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment > 0.2 and price < 70.
